introduction.p: Let's begin by looking at some sets of vectors in \real^3. As we saw in the previous section, the span of a set of vectors in \real^3 will be either a line, a plane, or \real^3 itself.

statement.p:
Consider the following vectors in \real^3:
\vvec_1=\threevec{0}{-1}{2}, \vvec_2=\threevec{3}{1}{-1}, \vvec_3=\threevec{2}{0}{1} . Describe the span of these vectors, \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}, as a line, a plane, or \real^3.

solution.p:
We will construct the matrix whose columns are \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3:
\begin{bmatrix} 0 \amp 3 \amp 2 \\ -1 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 2 \amp -1 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix}.
Because there is a pivot in every row,
a previous Proposition tells us that \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3} = \real^3.

statement.p:
Now consider the set of vectors:
\wvec_1=\threevec{0}{-1}{2}, \wvec_2=\threevec{3}{1}{-1}, \wvec_3=\threevec{3}{0}{1} . Describe the span of these vectors, \laspan{\wvec_1,\wvec_2,\wvec_3}, as a line, a plane, or \real^3.

solution.p:
Similarly,
\begin{bmatrix} 0 \amp 3 \amp 3 \\ -1 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 2 \amp -1 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}.
As there are two pivot positions, we see that \laspan{\wvec_1, \wvec_2, \wvec_3} is a plane in \real^3.

statement.p:
Show that the vector \wvec_3 is a linear combination of \wvec_1 and \wvec_2 by finding weights such that
\wvec_3 = c\wvec_1 + d\wvec_2 .

solution.p:
We see that
\left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} 0 \amp 3 \amp 3 \\ -1 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 2 \amp -1 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array} \right],
which tells us that \wvec_3 = \wvec_1 + \wvec_2.

statement.p:
Explain why any linear combination of \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3,
c_1\wvec_1 + c_2\wvec_2 + c_3\wvec_3
can be written as a linear combination of \wvec_1 and \wvec_2.

solution.p:
We have
c_1\wvec_1 + c_2\wvec_2 + c_3\wvec_3 = c_1\wvec_1 + c_2\wvec_2 + c_3(\wvec_1+\wvec_2)= (c_1+c_3)\wvec_1 + (c_2+c_3)\wvec_2.

answer.p:
We have
c_1\wvec_1 + c_2\wvec_2 + c_3\wvec_3 = c_1\wvec_1 + c_2\wvec_2 + c_3(\wvec_1+\wvec_2)= (c_1+c_3)\wvec_1 + (c_2+c_3)\wvec_2.

solution.p: Any linear combination of \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3 is itself a linear combination of \wvec_1 and \wvec_2.

answer.p: Any linear combination of \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3 is itself a linear combination of \wvec_1 and \wvec_2.
